# Best portable power station for camping

The best one depends on trip length. For most weekend camping, a small 250-500Wh unit is the best balance of weight and capacity. Prices below come from the review sites and may have changed.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 270-290Wh)
PowerStationGearLab's guide covers phones, lights, cameras and a CPAP for several nights in this class ([source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)):
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249) is their best overall. It is 288Wh and 8.3 lb. Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, which recharges faster but has a shorter warranty. The Plus is still sold through Amazon and other retailers.
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199) has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard model with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC" variant.
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299) has a 600W inverter and can expand to 572Wh.
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179) is the budget pick, with a 600W inverter.

Buy links: [PowerStationGearLab's picks](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) (each has a "Check price on Amazon" button).

## Mid-size, for a fridge, a few days or a bit more power
- **Bluetti AC180** has 1,152Wh, an 1,800W inverter and LiFePO4 cells, and weighs about 16 kg (35 lb). It lists at $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF. The listing says the code was tested in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21, but checkout has the final word. The $499 price is for the station only, with no solar panel. It has a 5-year warranty. [Buy at Bluetti](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) (affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you). [Details](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** was OutdoorGearLab's best value, at under $530 on sale. It weighs 25 lb, but its fan is noisy and its capacity is limited. [Review and price](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

## Extended off-grid trips
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** was OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping and scored highest in their testing (81). It measured 1,710Wh of usable output and weighs 39 lb. Its list price is $1,499, but it was recently under $900 on Amazon. It isn't expandable and can't run a space heater or electric burner for long. [Review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** was WIRED's best for camping at about $1,079. It is IP65-rated, has a 5-year warranty and weighs just under 40 lb. [Review](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** was TechRadar's pick for camping. [Review](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)

## Caveats
- Most of these sources earn affiliate commissions. The guide that ranks the small units is also a commission-based site, and I couldn't verify its testing.
- OutdoorGearLab scored the small Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) low in a field dominated by larger units. They are fine for phones and laptops but won't run much else.
- Turn off a CPAP's humidifier to stretch battery life. It can triple the draw.

If you tell me what you'll run (CPAP, fridge, laptop) and how many nights, I can narrow this to one pick.
